correctness.rationale: The exact two-prime practical-number criterion is verified in full-text literature. Splitting the count at the exact dyadic crossing gives two PNT-controlled geometric prime sums with constants \(4\) and \(2s\); all terms with odd-prime exponent at least \(2\) contribute only \(O(X^{1/3}\log X)\). The normalization and extrema are elementary consequences. A direct finite divisor-subset checker through \(500000\) found no criterion mismatch; it is used only as corroboration.
